Query PostgREST as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__postgrest.R
oauth_db_postgrest_api.Rd

Read PostgreSQL tables and views or call exposed functions through PostgREST, using the visitor's current bearer token for each request.

Usage

oauth_db_postgrest_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  schema = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 30,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

url

HTTPS PostgREST base URL, including a reverse proxy path if needed.

schema

Exposed PostgreSQL schema, or NULL for the server default.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one request, including its refresh retry.

ca_bundle

Optional path to a trusted CA certificate bundle.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

An R6 client with these methods:

  • $select(table, select = "*", filters = list(), order = NULL, limit = NULL, offset = NULL, count = NULL, raw = FALSE) reads one result page as a data frame. Filters use PostgREST expressions, for example list(country = "eq.NL").

  • $rpc(name, args = list(), raw = FALSE) calls an exposed database function with POST and returns its parsed JSON value.

  • $request(path, method = "GET", query = list(), body = NULL, prefer = NULL, raw = FALSE) sends a native PostgREST request. Supply path segments such as c("rpc", "my_function").

Details

The services-only PostgREST demo permits its exact loopback HTTP endpoint while the returned demo handle is active. All other endpoints require HTTPS. Stopping the demo revokes this exception for existing API clients too.

Configure a shinyOAuth client for the identity provider trusted by your PostgREST deployment. Its access token must be a JWT with the expected audience and role claims. PostgREST verifies the token; PostgreSQL grants and row-level security control which data the visitor can access.

Create the client inside server() and call its methods in render or reactive expressions. No PostgreSQL driver or native OAuth hook is needed. schema uses Accept-Profile for reads and Content-Profile for writes.

Each call pins its starting authorization, obtains a current access token, and discards responses after sign-out, account changes, or permission loss. GET and HEAD retry once after a 401 with a renewed token. POST, PATCH, PUT, and DELETE are never replayed automatically, including function calls.

Results and pagination

select() returns one page; the server can cap its size. Use limit, offset, and a deterministic order to page explicitly. Set count to "exact", "planned", or "estimated" to request a total.

raw = TRUE returns an httr2 response, including Content-Range; inspect it with httr2::resp_header(). Otherwise JSON is decoded with large integers preserved as strings. Embedded resources may become nested data frames or list columns. An empty selection returns a zero-column data frame. Dates and decimal strings keep the server's JSON representation.

See also

vignette("postgrest", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Other platform API clients: oauth_db_bigquery_api(), oauth_db_clickhouse_api(), oauth_db_cratedb_api(), oauth_db_databricks_api(), oauth_db_fabric_api(), oauth_db_libsql_api(), oauth_db_opensearch_api(), oauth_db_oracle_ords_api(), oauth_db_salesforce_api(), oauth_db_salesforce_data_cloud_api(), oauth_db_supabase_api()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
postgrest <- oauth_db_postgrest_api(auth$connection,
  url = "https://data.example.org", schema = "reporting")
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  postgrest$select("orders", filters = list(country = "eq.NL"),
    order = "id.asc", limit = 20L)
})
} # }
